claims.claim: Reviewers find that hand-to-hand combat is a standout feature, offering satisfying, brutal, and smooth melee mechanics with environmental takedowns and combos.

citations.review_text:
This game still holds up surprisingly well for something that originally came out in 2012. The story was entertaining from beginning to end, Wei Shen was a great protagonist, and the characters were memorable enough that I honestly wish the game had spent even more time developing some of them.

The combat was probably one of my favorite parts. Hand to hand fighting feels satisfying, driving around Hong Kong is fun, and the overall presentation has aged pretty well. The open world itself is where things feel a little more dated. There's plenty of side content scattered around the map, but most of it feels like something you do for extra XP, upgrades, or money rather than meaningful stories or quests. I ended up treating it more like a linear story driven game with an open world attached to it.

Overall it's a good game that still holds up remarkably well over a decade later. I enjoyed my time with it, and while I wish there was a little more depth to the world and characters, what's here is absolutely worth playing.

Amazing Open-World Crime Game

Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition is an amazing open-world game with a great story, fun combat, and a really interesting Hong Kong setting. The hand-to-hand combat is especially satisfying, and the driving and exploration make the city feel alive.

The story kept me interested, and the characters are memorable. I also really like how the game mixes undercover police work with the criminal world.

Even though the game is older, it still holds up really well. There are some dated graphics and occasional small issues, but they don't take away from the overall experience.

Definitely recommend it if you enjoy open-world games, action, crime stories, and great combat. One of the most underrated games I've played!

Played Sleeping Dogs for the first time in 2026, and honestly, this game still holds up really well.

The storyline was probably my favorite part. What I really liked was that the game kept getting better as it went on. The missions became more exciting, the story kept pulling me in, and the character development was actually good enough to make me care about what was happening.

And the fighting... absolutely loved it. The hand-to-hand combat is easily one of the best parts of the game. It feels satisfying, and beating the hell out of a group of enemies never really gets old.

My only real complaint is the lack of weapons. I would've liked to have the option to carry my own weapons around, but at the same time, I think this limitation actually makes the game more interesting. You're forced to rely on your fighting skills and whatever is around you instead of just pulling out a gun whenever things get difficult.

For a game this old, I was genuinely surprised by how exciting it remained throughout. Great story, great combat, solid character development, and surprisingly little of that "old game" feeling.

Definitely worth playing even in 2026. Recommended.

Hong Kong never hit this hard, and it never will again ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I went in expecting a GTA clone and walked out with one of the best combat systems in open-world gaming, period. The melee is Batman: Arkham-tier satisfying, grabbing dudes and slamming them through noodle stands, glass windows, literal cars, and it never gets old. Guns feel like an afterthought (in the best way) because you WANT to get in close and brawl.

Wei Shen might be one of the most underrated protagonists ever written into an open world game, the undercover cop story actually has stakes, actual character development, and doesn't just coast on "crime bad, guy does crime." Hong Kong itself is dense, vertical, alive, rooftops to parkour across, night markets, neon soaking every alley. It's a smaller map than GTA but it's used SO much better.

Add in the karaoke minigame (yes, really, and yes, it's incredible), cockfighting, street races that don't feel like filler, and a soundtrack that somehow slaps in 2012 and still slaps now, this game is criminally underplayed.

If you like Yakuza, Arkham combat, or just want an open world that doesn't overstay its welcome, Sleeping Dogs is essential. Rest in peace, United Front Games. You made something special. 🐉

Recommended: Absolutely.

sleeping dogs is an absolute gem and one of a kind. the story is amazing and honk kong overall is breathtaking and the most important thing obviously the combat. i can confidently say the combat is more satisfying than the arkham series and the subtle rpg elements make you want to play the game for more and more hours the side missions and the collectibles are fine and the customization dosent have that much variety. the gunplay can feel a bit awkward at times but they nailed the hong kong action movies feelings. 9/10

Just finished the main story in around 15 hours. I still have some police missions left, but honestly I enjoyed the gangster side way more.
The story is average not bad, but nothing mind blowing. The real reason to play this game is the combat. I've completed 25+ games, and Sleeping Dogs still has one of the most satisfying fighting systems I've ever played. The hand to hand combat feels brutal, smooth, and every fight is just fun. Pulling off combos, counters, and environmental takedowns never gets old.
If you're looking for an amazing story, this might not be it. But if you want to beat up enemies with one of the coolest combat systems in gaming, then definitely give Sleeping Dogs a try. The fighting alone makes it worth playing.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the hand-to-hand combat system as heavily reliant on counters, where players wait for an attacker to flash red and press the counter button, paired with environmental takedowns like throwing enemies into phone booths or furnaces.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: GTA but with martial arts!!

An open world GTA-like game where you play an undercover cop infiltrating the Triad. The story is good, though it is fairly predictable if you've seen any undercover cop media, but that kind of adds to the charm in my eyes. The combat is fun, with unlockable combos, and buffs from outfits, but it does have some early Assassin's Creed syndrome where the combat really is: wait for attacker to flash red, press the counter button, swing a couple times, repeat til dead. There are melee weapons which can be stolen from enemies and used a bit before they break, and guns that run out of ammo. Unfortunately (or fortunately if it's your thing) a lot of later missions devolve into gunfights, which is a shame since the main draw for a game like this is the martial arts, and not the shooting. Overall it's a fun game with a good story

Pros and Cons of playing this game;

Pros: Playing this game
Cons: Playing this game

Okay jokes aside..

It is honestly fascinating how Sleeping Dogs manages to be one of the most uniquely satisfying open-world games of its era, while simultaneously suffering from a massive crisis of identity at the same time.

If you’re stepping into this for the first time, the core hook is undeniable. The game nails the gritty, atmospheric vibe of a 2000s Hong Kong undercover cop thriller. The hand-to-hand combat is the absolute peak of the entire experience. It’s (relatively) fluid, punchy, and strikes the perfect balance between accessibility and pure satisfaction. Shoving a Triad’s face into a lit oven, a phone booth, or an AC fan never gets old. 

Add to that a genuinely atmospheric world design where North Point feels dirt-cheap and cramped compared to the sleek heights of Central, complete with faithful left-hand traffic that anyone from an RHD country will deeply appreciate, and you have a phenomenal setup.

The problems start showing up the deeper you get. Somewhere around the middle-to-late act, the game completely loses its mind and abandons what made it special. Instead of doubling down on the stellar martial arts, it forces you into being a generic, cover-shooter GTA-lite. And as someone who pays attention to firearms, the armory here is a hilarious, painful mess. Why on earth are street-level Hong Kong Triads (well 18k isn’t really street-level, nor the Sun on Yee) wielding NATO-spec military hardware like a BULLPUPPED G36, a standard-layout L85, and an MP7??? Where are the cheap Norinco knockoffs (say Type-56), or the iconic S&W Model 10 revolvers actually used by the HKPF at the time? To make it worse, the weapons have that greasy, over-glossed specular coating that makes them look like cheap metallic airsoft guns sprayed with glossy spray paint or something.

The presentation is just as much of a roller coaster. While the combat BGM pumps an insane amount of adre…

"A man who never eats a pork bun is never a whole man!"

After completely clearing out Hong Kong, snagging all 59 achievements, and running through every piece of DLC, I can confidently say that Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition remains one of the most criminally underappreciated open-world games on Steam.


The Good:
The Combat: The freeflow martial arts system is incredibly satisfying. Utilizing environmental takedowns (like throwing thugs into phone booths or furnaces) and beating enemies with a fish for the "A Slap in the Face" achievement never gets old.  

The Setting: The neon-soaked streets of Hong Kong feel authentic and vibrant. It's a massive breath of fresh air from the typical American cities usually featured in this genre.  

The Story: Wei Shen’s struggle between his loyalty to the police force and his growing bond with the Triads feels like playing through a classic 90s action movie. The voice acting and narrative tension are top-tier.  


The DLCs:
The Definitive Edition packs in all 24 post-launch DLCs, which offer some great diversions from the main campaign.  

Year of the Snake: Offers a solid, action-packed epilogue focusing heavily on Wei's police work.  

Nightmare in North Point: A goofy, supernatural B-movie expansion that throws Chinese folklore and demons at you. It’s slightly repetitive but a fun, spooky detour.

Zodiac Tournament: A fantastic, filter-heavy homage to classic 70s martial arts island-survival movies.


The 100% Achievement Grind:
If you're going for the full completion on Steam, brace yourself for a bit of a grind. The main story is paced perfectly, but hunting down every last lockbox, health shrine, and securing the 15 Gold Stat Awards will test your dedication. Grinding out the gambling stats in the cockfighting mini-games is definitely one of the most tedious hurdles. However, the huge upside is that there are no multiplayer, missable, or bugged achievements, making the journey to 59/59 straightf…

citations.review_text:
The main game is basically a love letter to Hong Kong cinema of the 80s and 90s, and that is where it shines the most. I love the setting, the atmosphere, and the whole world. It feels like playing through an old-school crime movie.

The combat is simple but flows really well, with plenty of environmental takedowns to make things more entertaining. Missions have a good amount of variety, shooting feels surprisingly good, and the arcade style driving fits the game perfectly.

It also knows when to stop. The main campaign is a good length and never really overstays its welcome. The DLC being mixed into the main progression can mess with the pacing a little, but overall it is a great ride from beginning to end.

Nightmare in North Point is a short but fun change of pace. I liked the Chinese ghost story theme and the changes to combat. Even little things like writing on enemies before finishing them off are a nice touch.

The second DLC is basically the closest thing I've played to an actual Police Story game. It has some fun moments, but the missions themselves are much more forgettable.

Overall, still a great game. The story, setting, combat and driving all come together really well, and the Hong Kong atmosphere carries it even further. If you like old Hong Kong action movies, this is an easy recommendation.

I'm glad I got this game for $2.99. I bought it because people praise it so much as a hidden gem that was supposed to kill GTA. I like the setting and the concept they were going for, story-wise. What kills me the most is the gameplay itself. The camera is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad, especially when driving omg. It just does its own thing. I could see it giving someone motion sickness at higher framerates. The driving mechanics are also clunky as hell. The combat is repetitive and clunky. I don't even think the enemies are hard, it's just the responsiveness of the button pressing feels delayed or nonexistent sometimes. What keeps me still playing is the story. It's not the most deep story, but for the cheap price, it's enough to keep me going. It's one of those games where I want to finish it just to say I played it.

I just finished the base game and the story was ok. I liked it but the pacing was off and feels kind of incomplete and/or rushed. The gameplay still sucked regardless and because of that, I don't even want to try the DLCs. I don't regret playing it, though. Still worth the $2.99.

People likes to compare this game to GTA. As someone whose open world experience is mostly from Rockstar games, this game is very different from GTA, seeing as it wasnt even trying to be one.

Gameplay wise the game is really good and fun to play. Rather than it feeling similar to GTA, it felt more like a combination of Bully and The Warriors, which both games i really love. That said, the driving in this game for me isnt the best because of how the cars handle. But to be fair, maybe its because im just used to GTA's driving physics.

There are a few gripes i have with this game, one of them is that i felt as if they couldve stretch out the last bit of the story just a little more, felt as if it ended too quickly. The ending does feel quite solid, because of all the loose ends being tied up nicely, its just that i feel like there couldve been more to it. Another thing they couldve done better is the girlfriends, you only went on one sidequest with all of them, and nothing else after that, not even a hangout. And lastly is the physics in this game, i mean it sometime is just funny to see the ragdoll, but it definitely couldve been improved. 

Overall id say this game is a solid 9/10. The story definitely isnt something to be impressed of, but it has a really fun gameplay mechanics that you wont find in any GTA game, such as the combo melee combat system and an XP system gained from finishing missions to upgrade your skill tree. The gunplay is also quite fun, even though it is very lacking at the beginning of the game, but you get more towards the end. Definitely an underrated game being overshadowed by GTA, even though as ive said that it is very much different when in comparison. Wasnt a huge fan at first but quickly fell in love with the game after a while. This game is definitely worth the time.

There is a solid if not perfect, pure action game, revolving around the martial arts-based, dynamic, [i]Arkham[/i]-esque combat system with delightfully brutal environmental finishers, taking inspiration from Hong Kong action cinema classics inside this rather lackluster open world game, which makes me wish someone would've interfered at one point to scale it back to that game in its development, because open world elements add near nothing of note to [i]Sleeping Dogs[/i].

Traversal isn't fun for example; driving lacks necessary and consistent physics to work properly and parkour --if you can even call it that-- feels stiff and unresponsive. Setting of Hong Kong --albeit being pretty to look at, seemingly authentic and comperatively fresh-- with its narrow roads, locales devoid of life and only a handful and repetitive side activities, doesn't offer much. There is not enough edge --or humor or grit or realism or spice, poison of your own choice really-- to be found in its worldbuilding. Dull presentation just makes a waste of superb voice acting from everybody involved. Shockingly, considering its inspirations and the themes at hand, story just reeks of banality; main character empty, side characters unexplored, antagonists one dimensional, clever writing to give said main character any proper, interesting or relatable motivation or the overall story some surprising twists and turns, non-existent. Cover-based TPS elements feel crammed in for no other reason than to draw in the usual open world crowd who just wanted something to pass to time with till next GTA came out, which is especially saddening because they could've just copied [i]Stranglehold[/i] one-to-one and call it a day, without any objections in my opinion. The gunplay is also quite fun, even though it is very lacking at the beginning of the game, but you get more towards the end. Definitely an underrated game being overshadowed by GTA, even though as ive said that it is very much different when in comparison. Wasnt a huge fan at first but quickly fell in love with the game after a while. This game is definitely worth the time.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the hand-to-hand combat system as heavily featuring martial arts with counter-attacks and environmental takedowns.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: GTA but with martial arts!!

An open world GTA-like game where you play an undercover cop infiltrating the Triad. The story is good, though it is fairly predictable if you've seen any undercover cop media, but that kind of adds to the charm in my eyes. The combat is fun, with unlockable combos, and buffs from outfits, but it does have some early Assassin's Creed syndrome where the combat really is: wait for attacker to flash red, press the counter button, swing a couple times, repeat til dead. There are melee weapons which can be stolen from enemies and used a bit before they break, and guns that run out of ammo. Unfortunately (or fortunately if it's your thing) a lot of later missions devolve into gunfights, which is a shame since the main draw for a game like this is the martial arts, and not the shooting. Overall it's a fun game with a good story

Came for the gta alternative, stayed for one of the coolest crime stories in gaming. counter-attacks during brawls feel super responsive and satisfying to land. action-hijacking moving cars on the highway will never fail to be badass. 
Hong Kong feels alive with all the street markets, radio stations, and ambient npc chatter. pacing is fast, mission variety is high, and the ending hits hard. worth buying this whether it is on sale or full price. 
Easily a solid 9/10.
Key game of my childhood. Still better than most AAA titles to this day!

Pros:

* This is essentially GTA IV but set in Hong Kong with a primarily Asian cast. It was developed by a now-defunct studio that included talent who had worked on games such as Bully, and the Rockstar influence is felt in everything about this game - from the living open world with many side missions and activities, to the great soundtrack and satirical spoken sections on the in-game radio stations

* Very strong video game story - it falls short of excellent, it's never moving or profound, but it does cloak-and-dagger very well and it has some quite interesting twists and turns, with enough narrative weight to keep it compelling throughout

* The combat is surprisingly fantastic, most fights are hand-to-hand and freeform, like a very satisfying mixture of elements of the Batman Arkham series and fighting games, plus some quick-time events involved. The game keeps introducing new martial arts moves right up until the end, so you're always trying something new and it makes the fighting never get stale

* There are multiple in-game karaoke bars, and the otherwise tough as nails protagonist will break out his falsetto to sing songs like Girls Just Want to Have Fun and Take on Me, and I cannot stress enough how hilarious it is, especially when you butcher it

Cons:

* Guns are conspicuously missing from the first part of the game and even after their introduction they're still heavily restricted. You can only ever carry one at a time and they're never permanently kept (starting up and ending most missions will delete whatever gun you had), you also can't buy them anywhere, they're basically a temporary power-up more than anything. The gunplay is decent but not outstanding so it's not a tragedy, but a gangster game where guns barely exist feels strange at times

* The driving really could've been better. It's not awful and you do get used to it, but it reminds me again of GTA IV and not in a good way. Many of the vehicles feel floaty and not perfectly responsive, and …

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world setting is based in Hong Kong, offering a dense environment with narrow roads and left-hand traffic that differs from typical American city settings.

citations.review_text:
Sleeping Dogs for many of the gamers remains memorable for its unique martial arts that was non existent in GTA type genres. The achievements in the game rewarded you generously allowing the player to level up their character. Some of the outfits actually help out Wei Shen in different types of stats whichever way the players would like. I espcially spent most of my time so far beating enemies with my fists. All the finishers ways to execute the enemy felt satisfying and rewarding. As for technically it holds up pretty well for its time. I understand this was released in 2014 but for a game that released in 2014 it works extremely well on high end devices without any old tech stutters. 

The game is set in Hong Kong, while its not a massive map and you can explore the entire map in maybe 1 hour, it is dense. You have crowds everywhere there is some activity going. You will never feel it is a dull moment in this game as devs made sure it feels like a lively city. 

The story is not your usual rags to riches story for a criminal. It follows an undercover cop who needs to take down one of the biggest gangs in the city. It is a rollercoaster for sure with some cinematic scenes in action and just gives off a very Hollywood-ish vibe.

Overall I recommend this game for those who would like a change from the gun fight and rather explore the fist fight aspect of this genre.

Pros and Cons of playing this game;

Pros: Playing this game
Cons: Playing this game

Okay jokes aside..

It is honestly fascinating how Sleeping Dogs manages to be one of the most uniquely satisfying open-world games of its era, while simultaneously suffering from a massive crisis of identity at the same time.

If you’re stepping into this for the first time, the core hook is undeniable. The game nails the gritty, atmospheric vibe of a 2000s Hong Kong undercover cop thriller. The hand-to-hand combat is the absolute peak of the entire experience. It’s (relatively) fluid, punchy, and strikes the perfect balance between accessibility and pure satisfaction. Shoving a Triad’s face into a lit oven, a phone booth, or an AC fan never gets old. 

Add to that a genuinely atmospheric world design where North Point feels dirt-cheap and cramped compared to the sleek heights of Central, complete with faithful left-hand traffic that anyone from an RHD country will deeply appreciate, and you have a phenomenal setup.

The problems start showing up the deeper you get. Somewhere around the middle-to-late act, the game completely loses its mind and abandons what made it special. Instead of doubling down on the stellar martial arts, it forces you into being a generic, cover-shooter GTA-lite. And as someone who pays attention to firearms, the armory here is a hilarious, painful mess. Why on earth are street-level Hong Kong Triads (well 18k isn’t really street-level, nor the Sun on Yee) wielding NATO-spec military hardware like a BULLPUPPED G36, a standard-layout L85, and an MP7??? Where are the cheap Norinco knockoffs (say Type-56), or the iconic S&W Model 10 revolvers actually used by the HKPF at the time? To make it worse, the weapons have that greasy, over-glossed specular coating that makes them look like cheap metallic airsoft guns sprayed with glossy spray paint or something.

The presentation is just as much of a roller coaster. While the combat BGM pumps an insane amount of adre…

After 100% the game, it is a masterpiece for open world crime based city games, here are some of things that are special or unique about this game compared to other games I've played like GTA or Saints row, or even Watch dogs 2, or Mafia 

-It takes place in Hong Kong, a far cry from the usual settings of the USA or any western country setting that is common for open world crime city games, this is most noticeable in the road direction of the cars being different, so if you are sick of the regular American enviorment's play this game

-If you are aware of the kung foo movies of the 90s, or Jackie Chan fights, fighting in this game feels like you are playing a kung foo movie with the environmental fighting and all

-The game allows you to kidnap people by putting them in the trunk, and also to put people in the back of a police car, so if you are looking to randomly role play as a police or such, you have freedom to do so with this game

-You play as a police officer an, it allows you to easily spawn in police cars, although this game doesen't feature a minigame like in GTA 4 when you enter a police car and you hunt down criminals, you still have police side quests placed around the map 


For some issues or nitpicks I had

-The story for this game was quite short, I also could not scratch my head at the choices and the random hostility made by Wei Shen, especially near the end

-You often find yourself carrying guns in the story missions, but for the most part carrying guns in this game is like disposing of a soda can, you often find weapons really disposable, and its very hard to find yourself carrying weapons in regular open world, as you cannot buy any guns, however finishing the game lends you a pistol in your apartments. 

I think that this can be blamed because of the fact you lack a inventory system with Wei Shen, and it makes sense for the beginning because its focused on hand to hand combat, but near the end game you often find enemies with guns and pistols…

one of the best open world games i've played.
hong kong is a really great setting for a game and this proved that
solid 8.5/10
